history: Named for the Twentieth Century Limited, the express train between New York and Chicago. Printed by C.A. Tuck in 1937.
whyItWorks: Cacao and lemon shouldn’t work. They do because the aperitif wine bridges them—the drink reads as chocolate-orange, not dessert.
steps: Shake all liquid ingredients hard with ice.
Express a lemon twist over the top.
techniqueNotes: White crème de cacao only—the dark version turns it muddy and sweet.
Lillet Blanc is the modern call; a blanc vermouth is closer to the original Kina Lillet than dry vermouth, so trim the cacao if using dry.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Citrus gin doubles down on the lemon.

substitutions.notes: Blanc vermouth is the better match; dry works but drinks sharper.

name: Twentieth Century
description: Gin, lemon and white crème de cacao—a chocolate sour that somehow tastes like citrus.
